entry.content:
Distributed-workloads: github actions pinned by mutable tag/branch, including third-party snyk/actions/setup@master
A flaw was found in distributed-workloads. A remote attacker could exploit a vulnerability in the pull_request_target workflow by submitting a specially crafted pull request. This workflow processes untrusted code from the pull request author while operating with the base repository's sensitive secrets, such as the SNYK_TOKEN, and its default write token. Consequently, an attacker could exfiltrate these secrets, leading to unauthorized access to the Snyk integration and potential control over the repository.

entry.title: CVE-2026-116779 · signalwire freeswitch · Exploited
entry.summary: Exploited · score 100/100. GitHub_M says exploited in the wild · Nov 5; 2 PoC repos (2 vetted) — unverified, may be malware; Critical 9.8 · network (v3.1); CISA SSVC: total technical impact
entry.content:
FreeSWITCH: Inbound SIP MESSAGE can select the api chat proto and run FreeSWITCH API commands
FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.3, sofia_presence_handle_sip_i_message() split the To user of an inbound SIP MESSAGE on a plus sign and treated the left side as a chat protocol selector. Selecting the api chat proto reached switch_api_execute(), allowing a peer whose MESSAGE was accepted to run FreeSWITCH API commands, including operating-system command sinks, with the daemon's privileges. Inbound chat is enabled on the stock internal and external profiles, and any authenticated profile account is sufficient; stock directory users without password material can also remove that barrier in affected configurations. The flaw permits configuration and credential disclosure, arbitrary call control, and command execution, and exploitation has been observed in the wild. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.3.

entry.title: CVE-2026-69137 · SuiteCRM SuiteCRM · Likely next
entry.summary: Likely next · score 40/100. Nuclei template (http · high): scannable at scale; High 7.7 · network (v3.1); Part of GitHub bulk release · Nov 5 (155); EPSS 3.8% · 89th pct · day 1 — too new to trust
entry.content:
SuiteCRM: Authenticated SSRF in CalendarAccount testConnection Allows Internal Network Access and Response Disclosure
SuiteCRM is an open-source, enterprise-ready Customer Relationship Management (CRM) software application. Prior to 7.15.2 and 8.10.2, the CalendarAccount testConnection action passes an authenticated caller's server_url directly to curl without host, address, or scheme validation. The affected flow begins at CalendarAccount::action_testConnection and uses server_url, CalDAVProvider::makeCalDAVRequest(), and PROPFIND to carry attacker-controlled data or authorization state into the security-sensitive operation. The server sends a PROPFIND request from its network context and returns non-success response bodies, enabling internal-service access, partial response disclosure, service enumeration, and possible cloud metadata access. This issue is fixed in versions 7.15.2 and 8.10.2.

entry.summary: Likely next · score 52/100. Critical 9.8 · network (v3.1); Product in KEV (×3): Apache OFBiz; CISA SSVC: total technical impact; CISA SSVC: automatable
entry.content:
Apache OFBiz: externalLoginKey honoured pre-auth, reusable and unbound
Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay in ExternalLoginKeysManager in Apache OFBiz 24.09 before 24.09.08 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker who captures a live externalLoginKey value to obtain a complete, cookie-free, reusable session as the user who issued it, in every webapp that user can reach, because checkExternalLoginKey runs as a global preprocessor ahead of both the CSRF and authentication checks and accepts the key as a bearer credential that is never bound to a client, never expires, and is not invalidated after use, while the framework itself both appends live keys to every cross-webapp link it renders and, via WidgetWorker's unvalidated inter-app link target, lets an authenticated user's key be attached to an attacker-chosen absolute URL and delivered directly to the attacker's own server. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 24.09.08, which fixes this issue.

Apache OFBiz: Unauthenticated RCE via login-page widget injection
Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection') in Apache OFBiz 24.09 before 24.09.08 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server by staging crafted widget XML in a multipart upload and overriding the mainDecoratorLocation used by a manager login route through an anonymous JSON request, causing OFBiz to load the staged XML through its live screen descriptor mechanism and evaluate an unsandboxed Groovy expression while rendering the authentication-failure page. -- The exploit does not require a malformed or incomplete multipart body: a well-formed multipart request that is kept in flight and then allowed to complete normally is sufficient.
-- The screen loader reads the widget XML from a live process file descriptor while the upload is streaming, rather than from any file the attacker persists to disk.

entry.summary: Likely next · score 50/100. Critical 9.1 · network (v3.1); CISA SSVC: total technical impact; Vendor in KEV (×9): Red Hat; CISA SSVC: automatable
entry.content:
Keycloak-services: keycloak-services: saml redirect binding signature bypass via percent-encoded parameter names
A flaw was found in the SAML HTTP-Redirect binding implementation of Keycloak. The issue occurs because the server processes percent-encoded parameter names (like %53AMLResponse) while the signature verification logic only checks literal parameter names. An attacker can use this discrepancy to provide a crafted, unsigned SAML message that the server processes instead of a legitimately signed one, leading to full account takeover of federated users.

entry.title: CVE-2026-73099 · Apache Software Foundation Apache Juneau · Likely next
entry.summary: Likely next · score 50/100. Critical 10.0 · network (v4.0); CISA SSVC: total technical impact; Vendor in KEV (×41): Apache; CISA SSVC: automatable
entry.content:
Apache Juneau: Cross-site request forgery via default-enabled content query-parameter body override
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in Apache Juneau.
The REST server accepts a "content" query parameter that replaces the request body, and this is enabled by default on every HTTP method, including GET. A cross-site link can therefore deliver an attacker-chosen request body to an endpoint without a CORS preflight, defeating protections that rely on the HTTP method or content type instead of an anti-CSRF token.
This issue affects Apache Juneau: through 9.2.0.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 9.2.1, which fixes the issue. Applications that do not use the content parameter can also set disableContentParam to true.

Apache Juneau: Unsafe reflection allows attacker-controlled class initialization during parsing
Improper control of dynamically-loaded code vulnerability in Apache Juneau.
When Apache Juneau parses a value into a property of type java.lang.Class (including parameterized forms), the default class swap loaded the named class with initialization enabled, so input naming a class on the application classpath ran that class's static initializer. The impact depends on the classes present in the deployment.
This issue affects Apache Juneau: through 9.2.0.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 9.2.1, which fixes the issue.

entry.title: CVE-2026-102895 · gpustack gpustack · Exploited
entry.summary: Exploited · score 100/100. GitHub_M says exploited in the wild · Nov 4; Critical 9.8 · network (v3.1); CISA SSVC: total technical impact; CISA SSVC: automatable
entry.content:
GPUStack: Authentication bypass via trusted loopback source (reverse-proxy TCP peer or X-GPUStack-Real-IP header) grants unauthenticated admin
GPUStack is an open-source GPU cluster manager for AI model serving and GPU instance provisioning. Prior to 2.2.0, get_current_user in gpustack/api/auth.py treated a loopback request source as the built-in administrator when force_auth_localhost was false, which was the default. A remote request could appear to originate from 127.0.0.1 because client_ip_getter accepted a same-host reverse proxy peer or a client-supplied X-GPUStack-Real-IP loopback value. The bypass allowed unauthenticated administrative access, including user and model changes, persistent administrator API-key creation, disclosure of worker and cloud-provider secrets, and code execution through POST /v2/inference-backends/from-yaml. Exploitation was observed in the wild against a 2.1.1 deployment. This issue is fixed in version 2.2.0.

Zulip: Custom profile fields can be read by logged-out visitors in organization with web-public channels
Zulip is an open-source team collaboration tool. From 11.0 until 12.2, organizations with web-public channels enabled exposed the GET /json/users endpoint to logged-out spectators, and a missing access-control check allowed include_custom_profile_fields=true to return every user's custom profile field values in addition to the documented limited directory data. This exposed those custom profile field values to unauthenticated visitors. This issue is fixed in version 12.2.

Gitea public-only package token access to private OCI blobs
The OCI registry's cross-repository blob mount checked the target package against the token's `public-only` restriction, but checked the source blob only against the full account permissions of the token owner. A `public-only` token with `write:package` scope, whose owner can read a private package and write to a public package namespace, could mount a blob of the private package into the public package. The private blob, such as a container layer, could then be downloaded by anyone through the public package.

entry.content:
Gitea public-only token bypass through Actions runner registration
Gitea did not reject personal access tokens restricted to public resources (`public-only`) on the organization Actions runner registration-token endpoint, and the runner registered with the resulting token was not limited to public repositories. Holding only such a token with `write:organization` that belongs to an owner of a public organization, an attacker could register an organization-level runner and receive jobs of the organization's private repositories that have Actions enabled, including the workflow content, Actions secrets and variables, and a task token with access to the private repository. The issue widens what the restricted token can reach; it gives nothing beyond what the owner's full account can already do.

entry.content:
Gitea OAuth2 account auto-linking takeover through the sign-up form
When `[oauth2_client].ACCOUNT_LINKING` is set to `auto` (not the default) and registration is enabled, the link-account sign-up form looked up the existing account to link by the user name or email submitted in the form instead of the identity asserted by the OAuth2 provider. An attacker with an account on a configured OAuth2 provider could submit another user's name, link their external identity to that Gitea account and be signed in as it without its password, including as an administrator. The link persisted for later sign-ins. Automatic linking now only happens when the existing account matches the provider's email or provider-derived user name; otherwise the account password is required.

entry.title: CVE-2026-114230 · Apache Software Foundation Apache Qpid Proton C · Likely next
entry.summary: Likely next · score 50/100. Critical 9.8 · network (v3.1); CISA SSVC: total technical impact; Vendor in KEV (×41): Apache; CISA SSVC: automatable
entry.content:
Apache Qpid Proton C: Potential authentication bypass: regular AMQP frames can be sent as SASL frames
When dispatching SASL frames to authenticate the peer, Proton will also dispatch AMQP frames if they claim to be SASL frames. This allows authentication bypass. However there will be no user name set so the effects depend on how the application deals with this condition - which otherwise means that authentication has not completed yet.
This issue affects Apache Qpid Proton C: through 0.40.0.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.41.1, which fixes the issue.

Apache Qpid Proton C: Unbounded recursion in parsing AMQP message bodies can lead to crash
A message body that is deeply nested and decoded by pn_message_body() could overflow the stack and cause a crash.
This issue affects Apache Qpid Proton C: through 0.40.0.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.41.1, which fixes the issue.

entry.title: CVE-2026-105031 · Apache Software Foundation Apache Qpid Proton C · Likely next
entry.summary: Likely next · score 50/100. Critical 9.1 · network (v3.1); CISA SSVC: total technical impact; Vendor in KEV (×41): Apache; CISA SSVC: automatable
entry.content:
Apache Qpid Proton C: The OpenSSL TLS implementation adds a locally trusted certificate authority to the existing trusted system trust anchors.
When using the OpenSSL TLS implementation, both the pn_ssl_domain_set_trusted_ca_db() & pn_tls_config_set_trusted_certs() APIs added to rather than replaced the default system trust anchors. Leading to potentially trusting unexpected peer certificates.
This can be worked around by setting the SSL_CERT_FILE environment variable for the application to /dev/null.
This issue does not affect the Win32 SChannel TLS implementation.
This issue affects Apache Qpid Proton C: through 0.40.0.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.41.1, which fixes the issue.
